One thing I've noticed in the prop firm space:

A trader gets denied a payout for breaking a rule. The rule may be unpopular, confusing, or even a bad rule — but it was still a rule.

Then every trader who was denied for the same reason (or any other payout issue) joins the conversation. Suddenly it looks like an army of traders exposing a scam.

The problem is that social media naturally groups together people who had a negative outcome. Meanwhile, thousands of traders who passed verification, received payouts, or simply accepted their breach move on and stay silent.

I'm not saying firms are always right. Firms should keep improving transparency, simplify rules, and speed up support.

But calling every payout denial a scam without looking at the actual breach reason isn't fair either.

I've personally blown 80+ accounts of fp and goat  but never once expected a payout after violating a rule. Painful? Yes. Scam? No.

From my experience, Goat Funded Trader and Funding Pips both have been reliable. Goat can be slow at times, but they've remained consistent, transparent, and operational through every market condition.

At this point, I don't think there's a perfect solution for firms. If they enforce rules, people complain. If they don't enforce rules, the business model breaks.

Curious what the owners think about this dynamic because it seems every major prop firm eventually faces the exact same cycle.
